practiceNotes: This is a proposed prerequisite graph, not an applied curriculum or a certification of competence.

Use spaced repetition for definitions, representations, assumptions, mechanisms, counterexamples and method selection. Require separate assessment of proofs, derivations, code, experimental work and extended modeling.

Advance through prerequisite decks by demonstrated competence, including their performance tasks; outcome annotations explain dependencies but do not authorize skipping the rest of a prerequisite deck.

Wet chemistry, biological cultures, radiation, lasers, electrical apparatus and animal work require suitable facilities, risk assessment, supervision and applicable authorization. These conditions are not represented as already satisfied.

Human-participant studies and identifiable biological or behavioral data require applicable consent, privacy protections and ethics review. Use approved public or synthetic datasets when authorization is unavailable.
Security exercises must use isolated, explicitly authorized systems. Embedded and robotic exercises should begin in simulation or low-energy test environments.
Maintain reproducible notebooks, versioned code, uncertainty records and negative results. Assess transfer with unfamiliar examples rather than relying only on familiar flashcard prompts.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Living Systems

includes: Cells, organisms and biological scales; inheritance and evolution as introductory explanations; observation, hypothesis and evidence.

practice: Compare organisms and evaluate competing explanations using observations and simple evidence dossiers.

outcomes.description: Distinguish observations, hypotheses, mechanisms and evidence, including alternatives and uncertainty.
Distinguish cellular, organismal, population and ecosystem organization and explain emergent biological functions.
Explain inheritance, variation and natural selection conceptually without teleological reasoning.

decks.title: Arithmetic, Algebra and Functions

includes: Real arithmetic, units and ratios; equations and inequalities; functions, powers, logarithms and graphs.

practice: Solve mixed unit, proportional reasoning and equation-modeling problems; explain checks and domain restrictions.

outcomes.description: Solve and check linear, quadratic and simple exponential equations and inequalities.
Interpret and transform polynomial, exponential and logarithmic functions using formulas and graphs.
Calculate with fractions, decimals, signed numbers, scientific notation, ratios and dimensional units.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Matter, Atoms and Bonding

includes: Atoms, isotopes and periodicity; chemical formulas and structural representations; qualitative bonding, polarity and molecular geometry.

practice: Construct and critique molecular models and classify unknown substances from structural evidence.

outcomes.description: Explain atomic composition, isotopes and qualitative periodic trends using shell models and their limits.
Predict elementary molecular geometry, polarity and intermolecular interactions from explicit bonding models.
Translate between names, formulas, particle diagrams and Lewis structures.

decks.subject: computer-science

practice: Build tested text-processing and scientific-data programs from written specifications.

outcomes.description: Process collections and text or tabular files with explicit input validation.

Translate relational problems into directed, undirected and weighted graph models.
Apply and justify elementary matching, coloring and planarity criteria.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Group Theory

includes: Groups and actions; homomorphisms and quotients; finite-group structure and Sylow theorems.

practice: Prove structural results and classify groups under specified order constraints.

outcomes.description: Apply Lagrange, class-equation and Sylow arguments to classify small finite groups.
Construct groups and actions and use orbit-stabilizer reasoning in concrete examples.
Prove and apply homomorphism and quotient-group theorems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra

includes: Linear systems and matrices; vector spaces and linear maps; complex scalar arithmetic; eigenstructure, orthogonality and singular values.

practice: Combine hand matrix calculations with proofs about invariant subspaces and approximation.

outcomes.description: Solve linear systems and determine rank, null spaces and consistency by elimination.
Construct orthogonal projections, least-squares solutions and singular-value decompositions in small examples.
Compute eigenstructure and explain diagonalization and the finite-dimensional spectral theorem.
Prove statements about bases, dimension and linear maps over real and complex scalars.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Number Theory

includes: Divisibility and Diophantine equations; modular arithmetic; quadratic residues and reciprocity.

practice: Develop arithmetic proofs and efficient hand algorithms, including insolubility arguments.

outcomes.description: Solve congruences using Euclidean algorithms, Chinese remainders and modular exponentiation.
Prove divisibility results and solve elementary linear and selected nonlinear Diophantine equations.
Apply and prove elementary quadratic-residue results, including a reciprocity argument.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Set Theory

includes: ZFC axioms and foundational constructions; ordinals, cardinals and transfinite recursion; choice and equivalent principles.

practice: Write transfinite proofs and trace foundational assumptions in familiar mathematical theorems.

outcomes.description: Develop standard mathematical objects within axiomatic set theory and explain avoided paradoxes.
Prove standard equivalences of choice principles and identify where proofs depend on choice.
Prove results using ordinal arithmetic, cardinal comparisons and transfinite induction or recursion.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Introductory Statistics

includes: Sampling distributions using supplied normal and t reference tables; confidence intervals; hypothesis tests; randomization and causal limitations.

practice: Analyze small datasets with tables and calculators; critique published statistical claims.

outcomes.description: Perform elementary tests, calculate effect sizes and distinguish significance, power and multiplicity.
Construct and interpret elementary mean and proportion intervals under explicit sampling assumptions.
Design randomized or observational comparisons and identify confounding, selection bias and pseudoreplication.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Point-Set Topology

includes: Metric and topological spaces; product and quotient constructions; continuity, compactness and connectedness.

practice: Construct spaces separating topological properties and prove preservation theorems.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply compactness and connectedness results and distinguish relevant counterexamples.
Prove continuity and homeomorphism statements using neighborhood and inverse-image definitions.
Construct and compare metric, product, subspace and quotient topologies.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Elementary Mechanics
decks.description: An algebraic entry into physical dynamics.

includes: Position, velocity and constant acceleration; Newtonian free-body models; elementary energy and momentum conservation.

practice: Solve and test elementary motion models and explain common force and energy misconceptions.

outcomes.description: Apply algebraic energy and momentum balances and distinguish system boundaries and external transfers.
Construct free-body diagrams and solve elementary equilibrium and constant-force problems.
Interpret motion graphs and solve constant-acceleration and projectile models with consistent coordinates.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Measurement
decks.description: Evidence and uncertainty in physical experiments.

includes: Physical instruments and calibration; dimensions and scaling; experimental comparison of simple models.

practice: Conduct low-risk motion, length and timing experiments and produce a model-comparison report.

outcomes.description: Use dimensions, scaling and limiting cases to construct and reject physical models.
Compare measured relationships with predictions using plots, residuals and uncertainty bounds.
Select and calibrate elementary physical instruments and document resolution, bias and uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Comparative Animal Anatomy

includes: Comparative animal body organization; tissue histology; organ architecture and structure-function relationships.

practice: Produce comparative anatomical and histological analyses using models, images and authorized specimens.

outcomes.description: Compare symmetry, segmentation, body cavities and support systems across representative animals.
Relate digestive, circulatory, respiratory, excretory, endocrine and reproductive architectures to functional constraints.
Identify epithelial, connective, muscular and neural tissues from calibrated histological evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology

includes: Population demography using discrete balances; species interactions and communities; energy flow, productivity and environmental gradients.

practice: Analyze field population and community datasets and construct accountable ecosystem energy budgets.

outcomes.description: Explain competition, predation, mutualism and community assembly using observational and experimental evidence.
Compare productivity, trophic transfer and nutrient limitation across terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
Analyze life tables and discrete population balances and explain density dependence and dispersal.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Experimental Biology
decks.description: Design and interpretation of biological investigations.

includes: Biological controls and replication; inferential comparisons and causal limitations; reproducible protocols and data records.

practice: Design and analyze a controlled growth or observational field investigation and critique its causal limits.

outcomes.description: Design biological experiments with appropriate controls, randomization, blocking and independent replication.
Interpret effect estimates and uncertainty while identifying confounding and alternative biological mechanisms.
Produce reproducible protocols, raw-data records and transparent reports including exclusions and negative results.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics

includes: Meiosis and Mendelian transmission; linkage and recombination; chromosome variation, pedigrees and genetic interactions.

practice: Solve cross and pedigree problems and distinguish genetic models using supplied offspring data.

outcomes.description: Explain chromosome-number and structural variation and predict transmission and phenotypic consequences.
Infer linkage and recombination maps from crosses and identify limits of mapping resolution.
Derive inheritance probabilities from meiosis and analyze pedigrees with dominance, penetrance and interaction assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology
decks.description: Microorganisms as organisms and interacting populations.

includes: Microbial growth and metabolic diversity; bacterial and archaeal structure; ecological and pathogenic interactions; culture and susceptibility methods.

practice: Analyze or safely perform nonpathogenic growth and susceptibility investigations with contamination controls.

outcomes.description: Design aseptic culture, enumeration and susceptibility assays with valid controls and containment.
Compare bacterial and archaeal structures, metabolism and genetic exchange using organismal evidence.
Calculate microbial growth and dilution relationships and explain nutrient and environmental limitations.
Explain microbial symbiosis, biofilms, pathogenesis and antimicrobial-resistance mechanisms.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Equilibria

includes: Mass-action equilibrium and reaction quotients; acid-base equilibria and buffers; solubility and complexation with mass and charge balances.

practice: Solve coupled speciation problems and compare exact algebraic solutions with common approximations.

outcomes.description: Calculate pH, buffer behavior and titration speciation for elementary acid-base systems.
Formulate equilibrium, mass-balance and charge-balance equations and validate simplifying approximations.
Calculate coupled solubility and complexation equilibria and predict selective precipitation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics
decks.description: Rates and evidence for reaction pathways.

includes: Empirical rate laws; supplied integrated rate models and Arrhenius relations; mechanistic and catalytic evidence.

practice: Analyze time-course data and design experiments that discriminate competing kinetic mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Fit and interpret zero-, first- and second-order integrated models and temperature dependence.
Test elementary mechanism and catalyst proposals against rate laws, intermediates and experimental perturbations.
Infer rate orders and constants from concentration-rate data and distinguish rate from stoichiometry.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Foundations

includes: Chemical hazards and waste; weighing, volumetry and titration; filtration, extraction and distillation.

practice: Complete supervised solution preparation, titration and separation investigations with auditable notebooks.

outcomes.description: Interpret safety information and design supervised handling, containment and waste procedures.
Perform weighing, solution preparation and titration with calibration and uncertainty records.
Select and execute elementary separations based on phase and solubility differences.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Thermochemistry
decks.description: Chemical energy through an algebraic route.

includes: Heat, work and calorimetry using explicit constitutive models; Hess cycles; entropy and Gibbs feasibility at fixed conditions.

practice: Analyze calorimetry datasets and compare feasible, kinetically inhibited and temperature-dependent reactions.

outcomes.description: Calculate heat transfer using heat-capacity and calorimeter models and assess their assumptions.
Construct Hess cycles and calculate reaction enthalpies from thermochemical data.
Interpret entropy and Gibbs-energy changes and distinguish thermodynamic favorability from reaction rate.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Algorithms

includes: Divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic programming; graph algorithms; correctness and resource bounds.

practice: Solve unfamiliar algorithmic problems with implementations, correctness proofs and complexity analyses.

outcomes.description: Prove algorithm correctness and derive time and space bounds, including counterexamples to invalid strategies.
Design and compare divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic-programming solutions.
Implement traversal, shortest-path, spanning-tree and network-flow algorithms.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Database Systems
decks.description: Reliable storage and retrieval of structured data.

includes: Relational models, dependencies and SQL; indexing and query plans; transactions, isolation and recovery.

practice: Build a database application, inspect query plans and reproduce transaction anomalies.

outcomes.description: Compare index structures, join algorithms and query plans using explicit cost models.
Design normalized relational schemas and express constraints and queries in relational algebra and SQL.
Analyze serializability, isolation anomalies and logging-based transaction recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics

includes: Geometric transforms and camera projections; rasterization and visibility; meshes, curves and local shading models.

practice: Build a software renderer and assess geometric, sampling and shading artifacts.

outcomes.description: Construct coordinate transformations, camera projections and geometric representations.
Implement clipping, rasterization, visibility and interpolation in a rendering pipeline.
Represent curves and surfaces and apply explicitly bounded local illumination and texture models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction

includes: Human perception, attention and interaction models; user-centered prototyping; usability experiments and accessibility.

practice: Iteratively prototype an interface and conduct an approved accessibility and usability evaluation.

outcomes.description: Implement and evaluate interfaces against accessibility principles and diverse user requirements.
Use explicitly taught perception, attention and task models to design and prototype interactions.
Design usability studies and interpret performance and qualitative evidence without unsupported causal claims.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks

includes: Layered packet communication; addressing, routing and reliable transport; socket programming and traffic measurement.

practice: Build a reliable transfer protocol in simulation and explain packet traces under loss and congestion.

outcomes.description: Implement socket applications and measure latency, throughput and protocol failures.
Trace encapsulation, addressing and packet delivery across link, network and application layers.
Analyze routing, retransmission, flow control and congestion control under specified network conditions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Systems Programming

includes: C-style pointers and explicit storage management; process and file interfaces; threads, synchronization and data races.

practice: Implement a shell, a resource-owning library and a tested concurrent queue.

outcomes.description: Implement synchronized shared-memory tasks and diagnose deadlocks and data races.
Write memory-safe low-level programs using pointers, allocation, ownership and resource cleanup.
Use process, file and interprocess interfaces with robust error and lifetime handling.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Integral Calculus and Series

includes: Definite and improper integrals; fundamental theorem and integration techniques; sequences, convergence tests and power series.

practice: Solve accumulation problems and compare integral and series approximations with explicit error controls.

outcomes.description: Determine elementary sequence and series convergence and construct justified power-series approximations.
Evaluate definite and improper integrals using substitution, parts and the fundamental theorem.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Logic

includes: First-order syntax and semantics; soundness, completeness and compactness; arithmetic coding and incompleteness.

practice: Construct formal derivations, models and detailed metatheoretic proofs.

outcomes.description: Prove representative soundness, completeness and compactness results for first-order logic.
Formalize theories and distinguish syntactic derivability from semantic consequence.
Explain and reconstruct incompleteness arguments using effective axiomatization and arithmetic coding.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Representation Theory

includes: Finite-dimensional representations; irreducibility and characters; matrix Lie algebras and their representations.

practice: Build character tables and explicitly decompose representations of finite groups and low-rank Lie algebras.

outcomes.description: Prove character orthogonality and use character tables to decompose finite-group representations.
Construct and decompose group representations using invariant subspaces and intertwining maps.
Construct matrix Lie algebras and analyze elementary representations using commutators and weights.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Rings, Polynomials and Modules

includes: Rings, fields and ideals; polynomial factorization; modules and quotient constructions.

practice: Analyze unfamiliar rings and modules using explicit constructions and proofs.

outcomes.description: Use submodules, quotients and module homomorphisms and compare modules with vector spaces.
Prove and apply divisibility, irreducibility and unique-factorization results for polynomial rings.
Construct ring homomorphisms, ideals and quotient rings and prove basic isomorphism results.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Elementary Electric and Magnetic Fields

includes: Coulomb fields and electric potential for discrete charges; magnetic forces; flux and induction in elementary geometries.

practice: Solve charge and induction problems and compare field-line representations with quantitative predictions.

outcomes.description: Calculate discrete-charge fields and potentials and explain electric energy and conductor behavior.
Apply flux-change and induction models to simple loops and explain energy conservation and sign conventions.
Predict magnetic forces and charged-particle motion using vector directions and algebraic models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Geometrical Optics
decks.description: An accessible route to optical imaging.

includes: Reflection and refraction; lenses, mirrors and imaging instruments; aberrations, apertures and introductory resolution limits.

practice: Build or simulate imaging systems and measure magnification, focus and aberration.

outcomes.description: Analyze lens and mirror combinations, magnification and elementary microscope or telescope designs.
Diagnose aberration, aperture and ray-model limitations and distinguish them from detector errors.
Construct and calculate reflected and refracted ray paths and paraxial image formation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Special Relativity
decks.description: Space, time and motion beyond Galilean models.

includes: Lorentz transformations and simultaneity; Minkowski intervals and four-vector notation taught locally; relativistic energy and momentum.

practice: Resolve relativistic thought experiments using spacetime diagrams and invariant calculations.

outcomes.description: Derive Lorentz transformations and solve simultaneity, time-dilation and length-contraction problems.
Apply relativistic energy-momentum conservation to decays, collisions and threshold problems.
Calculate spacetime intervals and elementary four-vector invariants and classify causal relationships.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology
decks.description: Mechanisms and history of biological change.

includes: Selection, drift, mutation and gene flow; reproductive isolation and speciation; phylogenetic characters and historical evidence.

practice: Evaluate adaptive and nonadaptive explanations and reconstruct small phylogenies from character evidence.

outcomes.description: Distinguish evolutionary mechanisms and predict qualitative changes under specified population conditions.
Construct and interpret elementary phylogenies and distinguish homology, convergence and ancestral-state uncertainty.
Explain reproductive isolation and compare speciation hypotheses using genetic, ecological and fossil evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry

includes: Sampling and method validation; chromatography and extraction theory; gravimetric and titrimetric quantitative analysis.

practice: Validate an analytical method using blanks, standards, spikes and an independently characterized sample.

outcomes.description: Design sampling, calibration and validation procedures and calculate detection limits and uncertainty.
Perform gravimetric and titrimetric analyses with equilibrium and interference corrections.
Explain and optimize separation selectivity, partitioning and chromatographic resolution.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Main-Group Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Structure and reactivity across the elements.

includes: Main-group periodic chemistry; molecular and extended inorganic structures; acid-base and redox patterns.

practice: Develop element-comparison arguments and predict reactions of unfamiliar but structurally specified compounds.

outcomes.description: Predict inorganic acid-base and redox transformations and balance their chemical accounting.
Relate inorganic molecular and network structures to bonding, geometry and physical properties.
Explain representative main-group compounds and reactivity using periodic trends and bonding models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Mechanism Foundations

includes: Curved-arrow notation and electron conservation; organic acid-base reasoning; reaction coordinates and kinetic versus thermodynamic control.

practice: Repair invalid mechanisms and justify competing pathways from structure and energy evidence.

outcomes.description: Construct valid electron-flow steps and identify nucleophiles, electrophiles and bond changes.
Predict organic proton-transfer equilibria using resonance, induction and quantitative pKa comparisons.
Interpret reaction-coordinate diagrams and distinguish intermediates, transition states and control regimes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Search, Reasoning and Planning
decks.description: Symbolic methods for intelligent problem solving.

includes: Heuristic and adversarial search; constraint satisfaction; logical knowledge representation and planning.

practice: Build search, constraint and planning agents and evaluate failure cases on unfamiliar problem instances.

outcomes.description: Solve constraint-satisfaction problems using propagation, backtracking and consistency methods.
Implement heuristic and adversarial search and prove relevant admissibility or optimality properties.
Represent knowledge and action models and perform logical inference and symbolic planning.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compilers

includes: Lexing, parsing and semantic analysis; intermediate representations and dataflow; optimization and target code generation.

practice: Build and test a compiler for a small language, including optimization counterexamples.

outcomes.description: Generate executable target code with register allocation and validate translation behavior.
Implement lexical, syntactic and static-semantic analysis for a specified source language.
Construct intermediate representations and solve dataflow analyses for sound optimizations.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Complexity Theory

includes: Time and space complexity classes; completeness and hierarchy results; randomized computation and amplification.

practice: Develop full complexity reductions and prove simulation and amplification bounds.

outcomes.description: Prove NP-completeness and representative space-completeness results using polynomial reductions.
Compare deterministic, nondeterministic, time and space classes using simulations and hierarchy arguments.
Analyze randomized algorithms, error amplification and standard randomized complexity classes.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computational Geometry

includes: Robust orientation and intersection predicates; hulls and sweep algorithms; triangulation, Voronoi diagrams and spatial queries.

practice: Implement geometric algorithms and test collinear, coincident and nearly degenerate inputs.

outcomes.description: Design and prove convex-hull and plane-sweep algorithms with complexity bounds.
Implement geometric predicates with explicit degeneracy and numerical-robustness handling.
Construct triangulations and Voronoi-style decompositions and use them for spatial queries.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Cryptography

includes: Security games and reductions; symmetric encryption, hashes and authentication; public-key encryption, signatures and key agreement.

practice: Prove security claims for simplified constructions and implement educational schemes with attack demonstrations.

outcomes.description: Derive representative public-key schemes and assess their algebraic assumptions and attack models.
Formulate indistinguishability and unforgeability games and construct elementary reduction proofs.
Analyze symmetric constructions and distinguish confidentiality, integrity and collision resistance.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Verification

includes: Hoare and separation-style program logics; temporal logic and model checking; proof assistants and refinement proofs.

practice: Verify a small stateful program and protocol, preserving executable counterexamples for failed properties.

outcomes.description: Express temporal properties and implement finite-state model checking with counterexample extraction.
Specify program contracts and prove partial or total correctness using program logics.
Use a proof assistant to establish data-structure or program-refinement correctness.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems

includes: Scheduling and isolation; virtual memory and paging; file systems, crash consistency and storage allocation.

practice: Extend a teaching operating system and test isolation, scheduling and crash-recovery behavior.

outcomes.description: Design elementary file-system structures and reason about persistence and crash recovery.
Design scheduling and synchronization mechanisms and analyze fairness, isolation and deadlock.
Explain address translation and implement page-allocation or replacement policies.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel Computing

includes: Parallel decomposition and communication; shared-memory, message-passing and GPU models; scalability and performance measurement.

practice: Parallelize graph and matrix workloads and explain scaling limits using reproducible experiments.

outcomes.description: Design parallel decompositions and derive work, span and communication bounds.
Implement shared-memory, message-passing and accelerator kernels with correct synchronization.
Measure speedup and diagnose load imbalance, bandwidth limits and synchronization overhead.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Security

includes: Threat models and access control; memory and application vulnerabilities; authenticated protocols using explicitly specified cryptographic interfaces.

practice: Audit an isolated application and protocol, demonstrate authorized failures and verify mitigations.

outcomes.description: Use specified encryption, authentication and certificate interfaces correctly and diagnose protocol misuse.
Identify and repair memory, injection and resource-exhaustion vulnerabilities in sandboxed programs.
Construct threat models and design least-privilege, isolation and access-control policies.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology

includes: Homotopy and fundamental groups; covering spaces; chain complexes and elementary homology.

practice: Compute invariants of cell complexes and prove spaces are not homotopy equivalent.

outcomes.description: Relate covering spaces to subgroup structure and establish lifting properties.
Compute fundamental groups using homotopy and van Kampen arguments.
Construct chain complexes and compute elementary homology using exact sequences.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Commutative Algebra

includes: Localization and local rings; Noetherian modules and primary decomposition; integral extensions and dimension.

practice: Prove local-global statements and compute prime spectra and dimensions of explicit rings.

outcomes.description: Analyze integral extensions, prime chains and Krull dimension in standard examples.
Construct localizations and local rings and track ideals and modules under localization.
Prove Noetherian properties and use primary decomposition and finite-generation arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Fields and Galois Theory

includes: Algebraic and transcendental field extensions; separability and normality; Galois correspondence and solvability.

practice: Determine Galois groups and prove solvability or impossibility for explicit polynomial families.

outcomes.description: Construct field extensions and calculate degrees, minimal polynomials and splitting fields.
Prove and apply the Galois correspondence for finite Galois extensions.
Relate group structure to solvability by radicals and classical construction impossibilities.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Fourier and Laplace Methods
decks.description: Transform representations of signals and functions.

includes: Fourier series and orthogonality; Fourier transforms and convolution; Laplace transforms and derivative identities.

practice: Analyze piecewise signals and compare exact, truncated and sampled transform representations.

outcomes.description: Compute Fourier series and explain convergence, orthogonality and truncation artifacts.
Compute Fourier transforms and use convolution, sampling and frequency-domain identities.
Calculate Laplace transforms and inverses and derive transform rules for derivatives.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable Calculus

includes: Partial derivatives and Jacobians; multiple integrals and coordinate changes; constrained extrema.

practice: Model multivariate sensitivities, integrate nonrectangular regions and solve constrained resource problems.

outcomes.description: Classify unconstrained and equality-constrained extrema using Hessians and Lagrange multipliers.
Evaluate multiple integrals with appropriate domains and change-of-variable Jacobians.
Calculate gradients, Jacobians and Hessians and apply multivariate chain and implicit-function rules.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Ordinary Differential Equations

includes: First-order and second-order scalar ODEs; linear systems; existence, equilibria and local stability.

practice: Derive, solve and interpret dynamical models; compare stable, unstable and nonunique examples.

outcomes.description: Assess local existence, uniqueness and equilibrium stability using stated hypotheses and linearization.
Solve linear systems using eigenstructure and matrix exponentials, including forced systems.
Solve separable, linear and constant-coefficient scalar initial-value problems and check solutions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability with Calculus

includes: Continuous densities and expectations; joint distributions and transformations; laws of large numbers and central-limit approximations.

practice: Derive distributions and evaluate approximation quality analytically for finite sample sizes.

outcomes.description: Normalize common densities and calculate probabilities, moments and conditional densities.
Apply laws of large numbers and central-limit approximations and identify their limitations.
Derive distributions of transformed variables and sums using Jacobians and convolution in elementary cases.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis

includes: Completeness and metric limits; rigorous differential and Riemann integral calculus; pointwise and uniform convergence.

practice: Write theorem proofs and construct pathological sequences and functions.

outcomes.description: Distinguish pointwise and uniform convergence and justify exchanges of limits, derivatives and integrals.
Prove convergence and continuity results using completeness, compact intervals and epsilon arguments.
Prove central differentiation and Riemann integration theorems with explicit hypotheses.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astronomy

includes: Coordinates, fluxes, magnitudes and distance observations; celestial orbit models; planets, stars and galaxies from observational evidence.

practice: Analyze public imaging, transit and catalog data and document observational selection limits.

outcomes.description: Interpret astronomical coordinates, images, fluxes, magnitudes and elementary distance indicators.
Compare planetary, stellar and galactic populations while accounting for detection and selection effects.
Apply elementary orbital and transit models to solar-system and exoplanet observations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electric Circuits

includes: Kirchhoff laws and resistive networks; capacitors, inductors and stated transient models; safe low-voltage circuit measurement.

practice: Construct and characterize safe resistive and storage-element circuits with uncertainty and loading analysis.

outcomes.description: Use meters and oscilloscopes to measure low-voltage circuits and account for loading and bandwidth.
Solve resistive networks using current and voltage laws and calculate power and equivalent circuits.
Analyze capacitor and inductor energy and apply explicitly stated exponential transient models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Newtonian Mechanics

includes: Variable-force particle dynamics; work, impulse and conservation; rigid-body rotation; small oscillations and damping models.

practice: Derive and solve mechanical models and compare predictions with trajectory or oscillation data.

outcomes.description: Derive harmonic and damped oscillator models and verify supplied analytic solutions by differentiation.
Derive and solve particle equations for variable forces and elementary orbital or constrained motion.
Calculate inertia, torque and angular momentum and solve elementary rigid-body rotational problems.
Derive work-energy and impulse-momentum relations and apply them to extended systems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Phenomena

includes: Photoelectric, spectral and interference evidence; explicit two-state amplitude models; quantized atomic transitions and uncertainty.

practice: Analyze historical quantum experiments and solve two-path and two-state prediction problems.

outcomes.description: Apply quantized energy-transition and uncertainty models while identifying their domain and limitations.
Use photoelectric, diffraction and spectral evidence to distinguish classical and quantum explanations.
Calculate probabilities in explicitly taught two-state amplitude models and explain measurement and interference.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Behavioral Biology

includes: Proximate and ultimate behavioral explanation; learning, communication and social behavior; foraging, mating and behavioral study design.

practice: Conduct approved observational behavior coding and compare competing adaptive and learning hypotheses.

outcomes.description: Analyze foraging, mating, communication and social behavior using explicit fitness and tradeoff models.
Design ethograms and behavioral experiments that control observer bias, dependence and alternative explanations.
Distinguish developmental, physiological, functional and phylogenetic explanations of behavior.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biodiversity and Systematics
decks.description: Organismal diversity in an evolutionary framework.

includes: Taxonomic and phylogenetic classification; major microbial and eukaryotic lineages; diversity estimation and identification uncertainty.

practice: Construct an annotated local or digital biodiversity collection and justify classifications and sampling limits.

outcomes.description: Estimate and compare sampled diversity while accounting for effort, detection and taxonomic uncertainty.
Compare major bacterial, archaeal and eukaryotic lineages using distinctive structures and life histories.
Use keys and phylogenetic classification while distinguishing operational taxa and species concepts.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecosystem Biogeochemistry

includes: Carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus cycles; terrestrial and aquatic compartment budgets; disturbance, climate feedback and ecosystem limitation.

practice: Construct a watershed or ecosystem nutrient budget and assess sensitivity to disturbance and missing fluxes.

outcomes.description: Construct and solve ecosystem mass-balance and residence-time models with explicit boundaries.
Evaluate disturbance and climate-feedback hypotheses using flux, stoichiometric and ecological evidence.
Explain biological transformations and coupling of major elemental cycles across ecosystems.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology
decks.description: Applied protection and recovery of biodiversity.

includes: Extinction drivers and fragmentation; conservation decisions under uncertainty; restoration design and monitoring.

practice: Develop an evidence-based conservation and adaptive-monitoring plan for a specified landscape or species.

outcomes.description: Diagnose interacting biodiversity threats using demographic, evolutionary and landscape evidence.
Compare conservation actions using explicit objectives, uncertainty, ecological tradeoffs and stakeholder constraints.
Design restoration and monitoring plans with reference conditions, controls and measurable recovery criteria.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology

includes: Plant tissues and organs; alternation of generations and reproduction; water, mineral and assimilate transport; environmental physiology using bounded models.

practice: Compare plant anatomy and life cycles and conduct controlled germination or transpiration investigations.

outcomes.description: Interpret plant responses to light, nutrients, water and stress using controlled evidence.
Compare plant life cycles and explain reproductive and dispersal strategies.
Relate plant tissue and organ organization to growth and terrestrial adaptation.
Apply explicitly taught water-potential and source-sink models to plant transport and stomatal behavior.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population Genetics

includes: Hardy-Weinberg and allele-frequency recurrences; finite-population drift; migration, inbreeding and population structure.

practice: Derive allele-frequency models and interpret population data under alternative evolutionary mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Derive genotype equilibria and selection, mutation and migration recurrences and analyze simple fixed points.
Use finite sampling models to calculate drift variance and explain fixation and effective population size.
Calculate inbreeding and differentiation measures and assess demographic versus selective explanations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Biomolecules and Enzymes
decks.description: Shared chemical foundations of living matter.

includes: Protein, nucleic-acid, carbohydrate and lipid chemistry; folding and binding; enzyme mechanisms and Michaelis-Menten models.

practice: Analyze enzyme mechanisms, folding perturbations and kinetic datasets with explicit alternative explanations.

outcomes.description: Relate biomolecular functional groups and stereochemistry to polymer structure, interactions and chemical reactivity.
Construct acid-base, covalent, acyl-transfer and redox enzyme mechanisms with valid electron flow.
Derive the steady-state Michaelis-Menten relation algebraically and interpret inhibition and kinetic data.
Explain protein folding and binding using energetic, structural and environmental evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Coordination Chemistry
decks.description: Bonding and reactions of metal complexes.

includes: Coordination geometry and isomerism; explicit crystal- and ligand-field models; stability and ligand-exchange mechanisms.

practice: Interpret complex structures, spectra and exchange data and compare competing bonding explanations.

outcomes.description: Distinguish thermodynamic stability from kinetic inertness and analyze ligand-substitution pathways.
Determine coordination geometry, oxidation state, electron count and stereoisomerism.
Use specified ligand-field splitting models to predict spin, magnetism and qualitative spectra.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry

includes: Air, water and soil speciation; partitioning and algebraic compartment balances; pollutant measurement and source assessment.

practice: Analyze a watershed or urban-air case using chemical speciation, measured concentrations and mass balances.

outcomes.description: Design environmental sampling and analytical controls and distinguish source evidence from exposure claims.
Predict environmentally relevant acid-base, redox, sorption and complexation effects on chemical form.
Construct steady compartment balances and estimate residence times, partitioning and degradation under stated models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Instrumental Chemical Analysis

includes: Operational UV-visible and infrared models; elementary nuclear-spin resonance and chemical shifts; ionization, mass spectra and fragmentation.

practice: Determine unknown structures from complementary spectra and validate quantitative instrument measurements.

outcomes.description: Use a bounded spin-transition model to interpret elementary NMR shifts, integration and coupling.
Interpret mass spectra using ionization, isotope patterns and chemically justified fragmentation.
Use explicitly taught photon and vibrational models to interpret optical spectra and Beer-Lambert quantification.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Reactions
decks.description: Mechanistic theory of major reaction families.

includes: Substitution and elimination; alkene, alkyne and radical addition; carbonyl and acyl chemistry; aromatic substitution.

practice: Solve unfamiliar reaction problems and justify products, competing pathways and experimental discriminants.

outcomes.description: Derive polar and radical addition mechanisms and explain regioselectivity and stereoselectivity.
Explain aromaticity and predict electrophilic and nucleophilic aromatic substitutions.
Predict carbonyl addition, acyl substitution and enol-derived transformations with valid mechanisms.
Predict substitution and elimination pathways, rates and stereochemical outcomes from substrate and conditions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed Systems
decks.description: Correct services despite concurrency and failure.

includes: Distributed time and failure models; consensus and replication; consistency, partitioning and distributed transactions.

practice: Build a replicated service and use fault injection to test safety, liveness and recovery.

outcomes.description: Implement and justify a consensus-backed replicated state machine under crash failures.
Reason about causality, failure detectors and impossibility under specified synchrony assumptions.
Design distributed storage and transaction protocols with explicit consistency and availability tradeoffs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Embedded and Real-Time Systems
decks.description: Computation under physical and timing constraints.

includes: Microcontroller peripherals and interrupts; fixed-priority and deadline scheduling; resource, timing and fault assurance.

practice: Build or simulate a timed sensing system and verify deadlines, electrical limits and recovery behavior.

outcomes.description: Design watchdog, fault-handling and resource-control strategies and test timing violations.
Program interrupts, timers and digital or analog interfaces using explicit hardware specifications.
Calculate response-time and schedulability bounds for elementary real-time task sets.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Information Retrieval

includes: Text normalization and inverted indexes; vector and probabilistic ranking; relevance judgments and retrieval evaluation.

practice: Build a search engine and conduct a reproducible relevance and efficiency evaluation.

outcomes.description: Build compressed inverted indexes and efficient Boolean and ranked retrieval procedures.
Derive and compare vector-space and probabilistic relevance-ranking models.
Evaluate retrieval using relevance judgments, ranking metrics and statistically defensible comparisons.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Program Synthesis
decks.description: Research methods for constructing correct programs.

includes: Inductive and deductive synthesis specifications; constraint-based and counterexample-guided synthesis; correctness and search-space evaluation.

practice: Build a synthesizer for a small verified language and evaluate it on unseen specifications.

outcomes.description: Implement enumerative and counterexample-guided synthesis using locally taught SAT/SMT interfaces.
Prove candidate correctness and evaluate specification ambiguity, scalability and benchmark leakage.
Formulate synthesis tasks from examples, logical specifications and restricted program grammars.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Geometry

includes: Affine algebraic sets over algebraically closed fields; spectra and structure sheaves; local geometric properties.

practice: Develop varieties and schemes from explicit rings and prove local geometric statements.

outcomes.description: Relate polynomial ideals and affine varieties through Nullstellensatz arguments.
Use local rings to analyze dimension, tangent spaces and singularities.
Construct affine schemes and structure sheaves and explain gluing in elementary examples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis

includes: Complex differentiation and analytic functions; contour integration and Cauchy theory; Laurent expansions and residues.

practice: Prove analytic-function results and evaluate real and complex integrals by contour methods.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply Cauchy integral results on appropriately specified domains.
Determine holomorphicity and derive consequences of complex differentiability and power-series analyticity.
Classify singularities and use residues and analytic continuation in explicit problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry

includes: Smooth manifolds and tangent spaces; tensors, differential forms and metrics; connections, geodesics and curvature.

practice: Derive geometric quantities for surfaces and low-dimensional manifolds using multiple coordinate systems.

outcomes.description: Compute connections, geodesics and curvature and interpret intrinsic versus extrinsic geometry.
Construct manifold charts, tangent maps and vector fields and verify coordinate compatibility.
Calculate with tensors, differential forms and Riemannian or Lorentzian metrics.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Dynamical Systems

includes: Flows and invariant sets; local bifurcations; discrete maps, chaos and Lyapunov reasoning.

practice: Prove qualitative results and construct bifurcation diagrams for continuous and discrete systems.

outcomes.description: Derive normal forms for elementary bifurcations and classify parameter-dependent changes.
Analyze simple chaotic maps using periodic orbits, sensitivity and invariant-measure examples.
Analyze phase portraits, invariant sets and stability using linearization and Lyapunov functions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Information Theory
decks.description: Quantitative limits of representation and communication.

includes: Entropy, divergence and mutual information; lossless coding; discrete channel capacity and coding bounds.

practice: Derive coding bounds and solve source and channel design problems with explicit assumptions.

outcomes.description: Calculate simple channel capacities and explain converse and achievability reasoning.
Calculate information measures and prove their central inequalities in discrete models.
Construct prefix codes and derive source-coding bounds and typical-sequence arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure Theory

includes: Sigma-algebras and measures; Lebesgue integration and product measures; convergence theorems and Lp spaces.

practice: Write measure-theoretic proofs and construct examples separating convergence modes.

outcomes.description: Prove convergence results and compare almost-everywhere, measure and Lp convergence.
Define Lebesgue integration and apply Tonelli, Fubini and Radon-Nikodym results correctly.
Construct measures and measurable functions and prove elementary extension and product-measure results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Analysis

includes: Floating-point error and conditioning; numerical linear algebra; roots, interpolation and quadrature; numerical ODE integration.

practice: Build a tested numerical library and compare methods on well-conditioned, ill-conditioned and stiff problems.

outcomes.description: Implement root finding, interpolation and quadrature with error and convergence checks.
Distinguish conditioning, stability and truncation error and diagnose floating-point failures.
Implement and assess direct and iterative linear solvers and eigenvalue iterations.
Implement explicit and implicit ODE schemes and assess accuracy, stability and stiffness.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization

includes: Linear programming; gradient and Newton methods; convexity, optimality conditions and duality.

practice: Derive algorithms, solve optimization problems by hand and construct failures when assumptions are removed.

outcomes.description: Prove elementary convexity and duality results and apply KKT conditions with constraint qualifications.
Formulate and solve small linear programs and justify primal-dual certificates.
Derive gradient and Newton methods and analyze local convergence and constrained optimality.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations

includes: PDE classification and well-posedness; characteristics; separation and transform solutions for canonical equations.

practice: Derive classical solutions and test uniqueness, compatibility and limiting behavior.

outcomes.description: Solve first-order transport equations by characteristics and identify characteristic crossing.
Classify canonical PDEs and select compatible initial and boundary data.
Solve heat, wave and Laplace boundary problems using separation and Fourier methods.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Models

includes: Linear regression and ANOVA; generalized linear models and likelihood; hierarchical designs and model diagnostics.

practice: Work through small regression and design analyses, including hand iteration and model criticism.

outcomes.description: Formulate and fit small generalized linear models through likelihood and iterative equations.
Analyze blocking, repeated measures and elementary random-effects designs without pseudoreplication.
Derive least-squares estimators and interpret uncertainty, contrasts and residual diagnostics.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Stochastic Processes

includes: Discrete Markov chains; Poisson and continuous-time chains; stationary processes, covariance and spectra.

practice: Solve queueing, reliability and population-transition models and check long-run behavior.

outcomes.description: Derive Poisson-process identities and solve finite continuous-time chain models using generators.
Calculate hitting probabilities, recurrence classes and stationary laws for Markov chains.
Analyze stationarity, autocovariance and elementary autoregressive processes.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Vector Calculus

includes: Vector fields, divergence and curl; oriented line and surface integrals; Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems.

practice: Solve the same field problem directly and through integral theorems; diagnose orientation errors.

outcomes.description: Apply and explain Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems, including regularity and boundary conditions.
Parameterize curves and surfaces and calculate oriented circulation and flux integrals.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics

includes: Variational principles and constrained Lagrangian dynamics; Hamiltonian mechanics; canonical transformations and integrable motion.

practice: Derive equivalent dynamical formulations and analyze constrained and coupled mechanical systems.

outcomes.description: Use canonical transformations and action-angle variables in elementary integrable systems.
Construct Hamiltonians and analyze phase-space flow and Poisson brackets.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations and conservation laws for constrained mechanical systems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Control Theory
decks.description: Reusable theory for regulated dynamical systems.

includes: State-space and transfer-function models; controllability and observability; feedback stability and controller design.

practice: Derive and tune controllers for supplied plant models using hand calculations and explicit performance bounds.

outcomes.description: Design PID and state-feedback controllers for specified models and evaluate tracking and disturbance tradeoffs.
Analyze closed-loop stability and robustness using poles, frequency response and stability margins.
Convert explicit dynamical models between state-space and transfer representations and assess controllability and observability.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electronics
decks.description: Electronic systems for amplification and measurement.

includes: AC response and filters; bounded diode, transistor and amplifier models; sampling, conversion and acquisition electronics.

practice: Build or simulate a sensor amplifier and acquisition chain and characterize its response and failures.

outcomes.description: Design amplifiers and switching circuits using explicit device models and assess nonlinear limits.
Design elementary acquisition chains and analyze sampling, quantization, loading and bandwidth.
Derive transient and frequency responses of linear circuits using differential and transform methods.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics

includes: Hilbert-space operators and measurement; one-dimensional Schrodinger problems; orbital and spin angular momentum and tensor products; variational and elementary perturbative methods.

practice: Derive spectra and measurement predictions and compare exact and approximate quantum solutions.

outcomes.description: Use angular-momentum algebra, spin and tensor-product states in elementary atomic and coupled-state problems.
Apply variational and nondegenerate perturbative approximations and assess their validity.
Calculate state evolution, measurement probabilities and uncertainty using finite and wavefunction operator representations.
Solve canonical one-dimensional Schrodinger boundary problems and interpret bound states and tunneling.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermal Physics
decks.description: Macroscopic thermal behavior and microscopic interpretation.

includes: Temperature, heat and thermodynamic laws; gas processes, cycles and entropy; elementary kinetic-gas and equipartition models.

practice: Analyze thermal cycles and calorimetric data and compare microscopic and macroscopic energy accounting.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary kinetic-gas pressure and interpret equipartition and heat-capacity models with stated limits.
Apply the first and second laws with explicit system boundaries and reversible or irreversible processes.
Calculate work, heat, entropy changes and engine or refrigerator efficiencies for elementary cycles.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Waves and Acoustics
decks.description: Propagation and superposition across physical media.

includes: Harmonic and traveling-wave representations; interference, standing waves and resonance; acoustic intensity and Doppler models.

practice: Measure resonances and wave interference and explain deviations from ideal linear models.

outcomes.description: Apply acoustic intensity, impedance and Doppler models and identify their linear-regime limitations.
Relate amplitude, phase, frequency, wavelength and propagation speed in sinusoidal wave models.
Calculate interference, standing-wave modes and driven resonance in elementary systems.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Epidemiology
decks.description: Population inference about disease causes and spread.

includes: Disease-frequency and association measures; cohort, case-control and causal diagrams; elementary epidemic compartment models.

practice: Analyze an outbreak and an observational exposure study, separating mechanistic, statistical and causal claims.

outcomes.description: Design and critique epidemiological studies using locally taught causal diagrams, confounding and selection mechanisms.
Calculate incidence, prevalence, standardized rates and association measures with appropriate denominators.
Derive elementary epidemic models and interpret reproduction thresholds, interventions and model limitations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Fungi and Protists

includes: Fungal growth, nutrition and reproduction; protist cellular innovations and life cycles; parasitism, endosymbiosis and mutualism.

practice: Build comparative life-cycle explanations and identify organisms from microscopy and ecological evidence.

outcomes.description: Analyze fungal and protist symbioses and parasitic life histories using ecological and cellular evidence.
Explain fungal hyphal growth, nutritional modes and reproductive cycles across representative lineages.
Compare major protist cellular innovations, locomotion, trophic strategies and life cycles.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Metabolism and Bioenergetics

includes: Central carbon and biosynthetic pathways; respiratory and photosynthetic energy conversion; metabolic integration and regulation.

practice: Solve metabolic accounting and perturbation problems and explain pathway-level physiological failures.

outcomes.description: Explain respiratory and photosynthetic electron transport and chemiosmotic coupling with quantitative energy accounting.
Trace carbon, nitrogen and reducing equivalents through central catabolic and biosynthetic pathways.
Predict metabolic responses to nutrient, hormonal and environmental changes and identify consequences of pathway defects.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Genetics

includes: DNA replication, repair and recombination; transcription, RNA processing and translation; prokaryotic and eukaryotic gene regulation.

practice: Interpret molecular perturbation datasets and distinguish competing information-processing mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Trace gene expression through transcription, RNA processing and translation with mechanistic perturbation predictions.
Analyze regulatory circuits, chromatin and epigenetic mechanisms using causal molecular evidence.
Explain replication, repair and recombination mechanisms and predict genome-instability consequences.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cellular Physiology and Homeostasis

includes: Diffusion, osmosis and carrier transport; membrane potentials and excitable membranes; feedback, signaling and homeostatic set points.

practice: Interpret transport and electrophysiological traces and diagnose failures in simple homeostatic systems.

outcomes.description: Calculate equilibrium potentials with the stated Nernst model and explain action-potential mechanisms and limits.
Construct feedback models and distinguish regulated variables, effectors, compensation and control failure.
Apply explicitly defined diffusion, osmotic and transporter models to cellular flux and steady states.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population and Community Dynamics

includes: Matrix and differential population models; competition, predation and metapopulations; ecological model fitting and stability assessment.

practice: Derive and analyze population models and compare their predictions with supplied longitudinal data.

outcomes.description: Estimate simple ecological models and assess identifiability, residual structure and out-of-sample predictions.
Analyze interaction and metapopulation models for coexistence, cycles and extinction conditions.
Derive structured population models and calculate growth, sensitivities and demographic thresholds.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Quantitative Genetics and Breeding
decks.description: Genetics of complex traits and selection.

includes: Variance components and heritability; linkage and association mapping of traits; breeding values and selection response.

practice: Analyze pedigree or breeding-trial data and design a selection strategy with explicit uncertainty and welfare constraints.

outcomes.description: Derive elementary genetic variance decompositions and interpret heritability under specified environments and designs.
Predict selection response and design breeding comparisons accounting for inbreeding and genotype-environment interaction.
Analyze linkage and association evidence while controlling structure, relatedness and multiple comparisons.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology Foundations

includes: Macromolecular folds and assemblies; structure-function and conformational change; coordinate, map and restraint validation.

practice: Critique deposited structural models and propose experiments distinguishing alternative structure-function explanations.

outcomes.description: Analyze protein and nucleic-acid folds, interfaces and assemblies using molecular geometry.
Evaluate supplied coordinate models, maps and restraints for resolution, uncertainty and overinterpretation.
Relate structural changes to binding and catalysis while distinguishing static structures from dynamic mechanisms.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Synthesis

includes: Retrosynthetic disconnections; redox and protecting-group selectivity; enolate and organometallic carbon-carbon construction.

practice: Design and compare multistep routes with explicit selectivity, yield and hazard tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Plan carbon-carbon bond formation using enolate and elementary organometallic reagent chemistry.
Develop convergent retrosynthetic plans with justified functional-group and bond disconnections.
Select chemoselective redox and protection strategies and predict incompatibilities.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organometallic Chemistry and Catalysis

includes: Metal-carbon bonding and electron counting; elementary organometallic steps; homogeneous catalytic cycles and mechanistic selectivity.

practice: Reconstruct catalytic mechanisms and design experiments distinguishing resting states and rate-limiting steps.

outcomes.description: Construct and assess catalytic cycles using kinetics, selectivity and catalyst-deactivation evidence.
Predict oxidative addition, reductive elimination, insertion and elimination steps with mechanistic constraints.
Analyze organometallic bonding, electron counts and ligand effects on reactive configurations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry

includes: Step and chain polymerization; molecular-weight distributions; polymer architecture, transitions and structure-property relations.

practice: Analyze polymerization and molecular-weight data and design materials for specified property constraints.

outcomes.description: Calculate molecular-weight averages and dispersity from distributions and ideal polymerization models.
Relate architecture, intermolecular forces and processing to glass transitions, crystallinity and mechanical response.
Derive elementary step- and chain-growth relationships and predict architectural consequences of mechanisms.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry

includes: Atomic electronic structure; molecular orbital construction and symmetry; variational bonding and elementary many-electron approximations.

practice: Derive small-basis molecular calculations and compare quantum bonding models with chemical evidence.

outcomes.description: Derive atomic orbital and electron-configuration consequences with electron-interaction approximations made explicit.
Construct molecular orbitals and use symmetry and occupancy to predict bonding and reactivity.
Apply variational and linear-combination methods and assess their limitations for molecular energies.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning

includes: Learning objectives and generalization; linear and kernel methods; trees and ensembles; clustering and dimensionality reduction.

practice: Implement contrasting learners and produce an auditable evaluation on noisy, shifted and imbalanced datasets.

outcomes.description: Design leakage-resistant training and evaluation procedures and diagnose overfitting, shift and unfair performance.
Derive and implement regularized linear and kernel learning methods.
Implement decision trees and ensemble methods and explain their inductive biases.
Apply clustering and latent linear representations and assess identifiability and metric dependence.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Probabilistic Graphical Models

includes: Bayesian and Markov networks; variable elimination and message passing; Monte Carlo and variational inference.

practice: Build inference engines for latent-state models and compare exact and approximate posterior calculations.

outcomes.description: Implement Monte Carlo and variational approximations and assess convergence and approximation bias.
Implement exact inference using elimination and message passing and analyze computational cost.
Construct graphical factorizations and derive conditional-independence consequences.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis

includes: Banach and Hilbert spaces; duality and bounded-operator theorems; compact and self-adjoint spectral theory.

practice: Prove operator theorems and analyze integral operators and infinite-dimensional counterexamples.

outcomes.description: Prove completeness, projection and duality results in standard Banach and Hilbert spaces.
Apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness, open mapping and weak-convergence principles.
Analyze compact and self-adjoint operators and prove basic spectral decompositions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability Theory

includes: Measure-theoretic probability and conditioning; probabilistic convergence and limit theorems; martingales and stopping.

practice: Develop complete probabilistic proofs and counterexamples to invalid exchanges and stopping arguments.

outcomes.description: Construct conditional expectations and prove their defining identities and projection properties.
Apply martingale convergence and optional-stopping results with valid integrability conditions.
Prove representative laws of large numbers and central-limit results under explicit hypotheses.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics

includes: Degenerate and time-dependent perturbation theory; scattering and partial waves; density operators, entanglement and identical particles.

practice: Derive transition and scattering predictions and solve mixed-state and identical-particle problems.

outcomes.description: Use density operators and symmetrized states to analyze mixed states, entanglement and identical particles.
Derive degenerate and time-dependent perturbative predictions, transition rates and selection rules.
Calculate elementary scattering amplitudes and cross sections using Born and partial-wave methods.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astrophysics
decks.description: Physical modeling of stars and galaxies.

includes: Radiation and stellar structure models; stellar evolution and remnants using bounded microphysics; galaxy dynamics and mass inference.

practice: Derive stellar scaling models and analyze public stellar and galactic data against competing physical explanations.

outcomes.description: Analyze galactic orbital dynamics and infer mass distributions while assessing equilibrium and selection assumptions.
Explain stellar evolution and remnant formation using energy balance, nuclear-fuel and stated degeneracy models.
Derive elementary hydrostatic and radiative stellar-structure equations using explicitly specified opacity and energy models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Elasticity and Solid Mechanics
decks.description: Deformation and stability of solid continua.

includes: Stress and strain tensors; linear elastic constitutive laws and boundary problems; elastic energy, buckling and failure criteria.

practice: Derive deformation models and compare stiffness, buckling and failure predictions for simple structures.

outcomes.description: Solve elementary tension, torsion and bending boundary problems with compatible stress and displacement conditions.
Analyze elastic energy, buckling and elementary yield or fracture criteria with their limitations.
Derive small-strain kinematics and stress balance and distinguish isotropic and anisotropic constitutive laws.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electromagnetic Fields

includes: Electrostatic boundary-value problems; magnetostatics and materials; Maxwell equations and electromagnetic waves; elementary radiation.

practice: Derive and solve boundary and radiation problems with conservation and limiting-case checks.

outcomes.description: Solve electrostatic boundary problems using potentials, multipoles and uniqueness arguments.
Derive magnetostatic fields and analyze bound currents and linear magnetic media.
Derive wave, energy and boundary relations from Maxwell equations in vacuum and simple media.
Calculate elementary dipole radiation and distinguish near, intermediate and radiation fields.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics Methods

includes: Detector response and calibration; noise spectra, filtering and lock-in detection; model fitting and uncertainty budgets.

practice: Build a reproducible acquisition and analysis pipeline for a weak-signal experiment or instrument-equivalent dataset.

outcomes.description: Calibrate detector response and quantify nonlinearity, drift, efficiency and systematic uncertainty.
Analyze noise spectra and implement filtering or lock-in extraction without invalid sampling assumptions.
Fit physical models, propagate parameter uncertainty and distinguish statistical from systematic discrepancies.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluid Mechanics

includes: Continuum conservation and stress; Euler and Navier-Stokes equations; viscous flow, dimensionless groups and instability limits.

practice: Derive flow models and compare analytic solutions and scaling estimates with fluid-measurement data.

outcomes.description: Use nondimensionalization to assess regimes, boundary layers and the onset of instability or turbulence.
Derive mass, momentum and energy balances and explain constitutive and continuum assumptions.
Solve elementary inviscid and viscous flows with appropriate initial and boundary conditions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity

includes: Lorentzian spacetime and equivalence; Einstein equations and stress-energy; black-hole, weak-field and gravitational-wave solutions.

practice: Derive relativistic solutions and calculate observable orbital, lensing and wave effects.

outcomes.description: Derive Einstein equations from the stated field action and analyze stress-energy conservation.
Solve and interpret representative spherical, weak-field and linear gravitational-wave problems.
Relate local inertial motion, geodesics and tidal effects to Lorentzian geometry.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear Physics
decks.description: Structure and transformations of atomic nuclei.

includes: Nuclear binding and structure models; decay, scattering, fission and fusion; radiation interactions and detectors.

practice: Analyze nuclear spectra and reaction datasets and compare model explanations under radiation-safety constraints.

outcomes.description: Analyze decay chains and nuclear reaction energetics, thresholds and elementary cross-section models.
Compare liquid-drop and shell models and calculate elementary binding and nuclear-state consequences.
Explain radiation-matter interactions and interpret detector efficiency, resolution and counting uncertainty.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Elementary Particle Physics

includes: Standard Model particle content and interactions; conservation and discrete symmetries; relativistic collision and decay signatures.

practice: Reconstruct particle processes from event data and distinguish kinematic evidence from interaction-model assumptions.

outcomes.description: Calculate invariant masses, decay kinematics and thresholds and interpret elementary collision signatures.
Classify particles and interactions and explain the empirical organization of the Standard Model.
Apply conserved quantum numbers and discrete-symmetry tests to allowed and forbidden processes.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermodynamics

includes: Thermodynamic potentials and Legendre transforms; Maxwell and response relations; phase coexistence and stability.

practice: Prove thermodynamic identities and solve stability and phase-transition problems under different constraints.

outcomes.description: Analyze stability and phase coexistence using thermodynamic curvature and equilibrium conditions.
Derive Maxwell relations and connect heat capacities, compressibilities and expansion coefficients.
Derive thermodynamic potentials and select natural variables for constrained equilibrium problems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Wave Optics
decks.description: Wave foundations of imaging and interference.

includes: Scalar diffraction and Fourier optics; temporal and spatial coherence; transverse polarization and optical interference.

practice: Analyze diffraction and polarization experiments and quantify approximation and coherence limits.

outcomes.description: Calculate interference visibility from coherence models and distinguish temporal and spatial coherence.
Derive elementary diffraction and imaging relations using scalar wave and Fourier approximations.
Use transverse-field and Jones-vector models to analyze polarization transformations and measurements.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Bioinformatics

includes: Sequence alignment and scoring; genome assembly, annotation and comparative analysis; biological databases, provenance and validation.

practice: Implement sequence algorithms and analyze a public genome dataset with independent validation checks.

outcomes.description: Construct reproducible biological-data pipelines with provenance, reference controls and uncertainty checks.
Apply assembly, annotation and comparative-genome methods and diagnose repetitive and biased-data failures.
Implement alignment and probabilistic sequence-scoring methods and justify their biological assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cardiorespiratory Physiology
decks.description: Integrated transport of gases through animals.

includes: Pressure-flow circulation and cardiac function; ventilation and gas exchange; integrated oxygen delivery, exercise and failure.

practice: Solve oxygen-delivery and pressure-flow cases and interpret noninvasive physiological recordings.

outcomes.description: Use taught pressure-flow and cardiac-cycle models to explain circulation and hemodynamic regulation.
Integrate circulation and respiration to explain exercise, hypoxia, shock and compensatory limits.
Analyze ventilation, diffusion and gas transport using explicit partial-pressure and binding models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cryo-Electron Microscopy
decks.description: Structure inference from noisy electron images.

includes: Electron imaging and contrast-transfer models; particle alignment and three-dimensional reconstruction; heterogeneity and reconstruction validation.

practice: Reconstruct a simulated particle and critically reanalyze a public cryo-EM dataset.

outcomes.description: Assess resolution, preferred orientation, overfitting and conformational heterogeneity using independent data splits.
